options: The Global scope's internal name
The record that defines a scoped application's isolated namespace, with its own scope identifier
A table that stores every Business Rule on the instance regardless of scope
A setting that disables all custom tables on an instance
questions.explain: Each scoped application has a sys_scope record defining its own namespace, identified by a unique scope identifier.

questions.q: Why did Global scope become a problem as instances grew?
options: Global scope only allows read-only scripts
Global scope automatically deletes customizations after 90 days
Global customizations sprawl across the instance with no boundary, so two unrelated teams' tables, fields, or Script Includes with the same name collide
Global scope cannot contain any tables at all
questions.explain: With no namespace boundary, two unrelated customizations using the same name in Global can overwrite or break each other.

questions.q: A Fleet Management app with scope identifier `x_acme_fleet` has a table you name "Vehicle" in the UI. What is its real table name?
options: x_acme_fleet_vehicle
fleet_vehicle_x_acme
sys_scope_vehicle
vehicle
questions.explain: ServiceNow automatically prefixes the table name with the application's scope identifier.

questions.q: Why can a Visitor Management app and a Fleet Management app both have a table conceptually named "request" without any collision?
options: Each table's real name is prefixed with its own scope's identifier, so the full names are different even if the conceptual names match
Tables named "request" are automatically moved to Global scope
ServiceNow renames one of the two tables at random
Only one scoped application per instance is allowed to use the word "request"
questions.explain: The scope identifier baked into each real table name is what the platform uses to keep the two separate — it's enforced automatically, not by convention.

questions.q: By default, what happens when code in one scoped application tries to reach a Script Include defined in a different scoped application?
options: It automatically copies the Script Include into the calling scope
It always succeeds with no restriction
It is not reachable — scope isolates server-side code from other scopes unless something explicitly allows access
It succeeds only on Sundays
questions.explain: Isolation applies to access as well as naming — cross-scope access requires an explicit mechanism, covered in Lesson 21.
